analysis:
Reviewed the three modified Swift files: EnginePerformanceMeasurements.swift, EngineV2Bridge+Accounting.swift and EngineV2Bridge+Admission.swift. All changes are local performance-measurement and deadline-admission logic: out-of-order freshness (max(at, now) in Rate.observe, gated by keepsNewestObservationTime), new coversObservation/observationAge/firstTokenStepRows accessors, a per-step decode charge, an observedDecodeStep tracker, and a prefill-rate anchor for engines without a recovery probe. They do not touch the coordinator WebSocket, E2E encryption, keys, attestation, App Attest authorization, prefix-cache storage or fan helper, so TB-002, TB-009, TB-011 and T-041 are not affected. No plaintext prompt data, secrets or logging are added.

The only security-adjacent surface is availability and admission accuracy (T-010, T-029 in spirit). Freshness now follows the newest observation, which only lengthens evidence lifetime for late-arriving completed work. That is bounded by the 120s freshness window, and a stale old sample cannot rejuvenate a newer one. The wire sampleAge calculation uses max(0, ...), so it is safe. The new IsolatedPrefillAdmissionRate.resolve anchor path (Admission.swift lines 95-104) relies on calibratedIsolatedPrefillTps, macIdle and calibrationPosturePermitsWork. Those are defined outside the supplied diff, so I cannot confirm that the anchor cannot be abused by a malicious provider to inflate its advertised rates. The provider is already self-reporting these metrics, so this stays within existing trust assumptions rather than being a regression.

Open integration questions, none with a security conclusion: DeadlineAdmissionFixes.decodeCharge, CBv2DecodeRateShape, observedDecodeStep and IsolatedPrefillAdmissionRate are not visible, so their numeric edge cases (zero or overflow batch rows) were not verified. admissionFixes is also not visible. The Admission.swift head text was not supplied, only its patch.
